{{Top}} {{RepulsorliftVehicle |image=[[File:GPE-3130Podracer-CT.png]] |name=GPE-3130 Podracer |designer= |manufacturer=[[Galactic Power Engineering]]''[[Endless Vigil]]'' |line= |model=GPE-3130 |type=[[Podracer]] |cost=11,500 [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] |modifier= |sysmods= |length= |width= |height= |mass= |max accel= |speed= |max alt=50 [[meter]]s |maneuverability= |engine=*2 [[ThrustMaster 9000 aerospike rocket engine]]s *2 [[ramjet]] [[engine]]s |poweroutput= |power= |shield gen= |hull= |sensor=Close |target= |navigation= |avionics= |maincomp= |countermeasures= |armament=None |complement= |bays= |escapepods= |crew=1 [[pilot]] |skeleton= |passengers=0 |capacity= |cargohandling= |consumables= |lifesupport= |communications= |othersystems= |availability= |role=[[Podracing]] |firstuse= |retired= |affiliation= }} The '''GPE-3130 Podracer''', also known as the '''3130-series factory custom''', was a model of [[podracer]] built by [[Galactic Power Engineering]] and designed for little bar straight-line speed. Its high speed made it a terror on straight-line raceways with broad, gentle curves, but its twin [[ThrustMaster 9000 aerospike rocket engine]]s, augmented by a pair of smaller [[ramjet]] [[engine]]s, made it difficult to control in tight spaces or sharp corners. The vehicle was awkward-looking and its [[repulsorpod]] was uncomfortable with an unintuitive control layout. In [[32 BBY]], the [[Gran]] [[podracer]] [[Mawhonic]] [[pilot]]ed [[Mawhonic's Podracer|a]] GPE-3130 Podracer at the [[Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Podracing|podrace]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]. During the race he managed to trail behind the lead [[racer]], [[Sebulba]], but in the first lap he was knocked out of the race by the other pilot when he rammed Mawhonic's GPE-3130 into a cliff face in the [[Mushroom Mesa]] portion of the [[Mos Espa podrace circuit|circuit]]. During the [[Galactic Civil War]], the GPE-3130 Podracer cost 11,500 [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] and was hard to find for purchase. Despite an aggressive marketing campaign by its manufacturer, the vehicle was unpopular, although some small racing teams fielded it because it was one of the fastest and most affordable podracers on the market. ==Description==
[[File:GPE-3130PodracerScale-CL.png|thumb|right|300px|The GPE-3130 Podracer was equipped with two ThrustMaster 9000 aerospike rocket engines.]]
The GPE-3130 Podracer,{{ForceCollection|Mawhonic|star=1}} also known as the 3130-series factory custom, was a model of [[podracer]] that was powered by a pair of [[ThrustMaster 9000 aerospike rocket engine]]s that provided its primary thrust. It was also equipped with a pair of smaller [[ramjet]] [[engine]]s on nacelle-mounted outriggers that augmented the larger engines and provided short bursts of boost. A multitude of attitude jets that were scatter over the vehicle's hull were also powered by the ramjet engines, although the jets did little more than make noise. [[File:Mawhonic-DB.png|thumb|left|300px|The GPE-3130 Podracer had an uncomfortable cockpit with a unintuitive control scheme.]] Designed for straight-line speed and little else, the GPE-3130 was a terror on high-speed racetracks that consisted of long straightaways and broad, gentle curves; however, its raw speed and the power control curve of the aerospike [[Podracer engine|engines]] meant that it was incredibly hard to control, particularly when it came to sharp turns or tight spaces. Despite this, the vehicle had above average handling and average turbo, although it had very low resistance.''[[Star Wars Journeys: The Phantom Menace]]'' The vehicles engines required large amounts of maintenance and used a volatile [[fuel]] that would detonate at even the slightest provocation. Due to its flat-nosed, wedge-shaped primary engines and the much smaller ramjet engines, which were considered almost comical, the GPE-3130 was considered an awkward looking vehicle, although this was deceptive given its speed. The [[repulsorpod]]'s [[cockpit]]—attached by cables to the two engines as standard for a podracer—was also uncomfortable, with an unintuitive control layout that made it hard for the lone [[pilot]] to view various essential information including the podracer's altitude or airspeed when flying. The GPE-3130 had no armaments or passenger capacity, with only a close [[sensor]] range. It had a maximum altitude of fifty [[meter]]s. ==History== [[File:MawhonicBows-TPM.png|thumb|right|300px|Mawhonic is introduced at the Boonta Eve Classic.]] Despite its high speed and an aggressive marketing campaign by [[Galactic Power Engineering]], the manufacturer of the GPE-3130 Podracer and its engine, the vehicle was relatively unpopular. In [[32 BBY]], the [[Gran]] [[Podracer (profession)|podracer]] [[Mawhonic]] flew a [[Color|green]] GPE-3130 Podracer during the [[Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Podracing|race]] on the [[desert]] [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]. Prior to the race, his vehicle was stored in the left wing of the [[Mos Espa Arena hangar|pit hangar]] of the [[Mos Espa Grand Arena]],[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] then moved to the pole-position in the front row of the arena's starting grid, where he stood by his vehicle as two Gran [[Technician|mechanics]] worked on it.{{Film|I}} [[File:Mawhonic_podracer.png|thumb|left|300px|Mawhonic used a GPE-3130 Podracer in the Boonta Eve Classic.]] Once the race began, Mawhonic initially managed to tail just behind the [[Sebulba's Podracer|podracer]] of the [[Dug]] [[Sebulba]], who was in the lead, but in the [[Mushroom Mesa]] portion of the [[Mos Espa podrace circuit|circuit]], Sebulba rammed the Gran's GPE-3130 with his [[Plug-F Mammoth Split-X engine|engines]]. Taking his focus off the circuit, Mahwonic shook his fist at his competitor, but this gave Sebulba the opening he needed to ram the Gran's vehicle twice more, ultimately driving one of the aerojet engines into a cliff face and causing it to explode. Mahwonic's repulsorpod remained attached to the destroyed engine as it spiralled away, but the other engine continued on alone briefly before dropping to the floor and breaking apart as it tumbled through the sand. Sebulba was later knocked out of the race himself by the [[human]] [[Anakin Skywalker]], who went on to win. During the [[Galactic Civil War]] it was one of the stranger podracers on the market, but at 11,500 [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]], it was also one of the most affordable. Because of this and its relatively high speed when compared to the other available podracers, some smaller racing teams chose to field it, although the vehicle was hard to find for purchase. ==Behind the scenes== ===Filming information=== [[File:GPE-3130PodracerCockpitConcept-TPMIG.png|thumb|right|300px|Jay Shuster drew concept art of the GPE-3130 Podracer.]] The GPE-3130 Podracer was created for the [[prequel trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], which was released on [[May 19]], [[1999]].''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]'' Concept art of the vehicle's pod and engines was drawn by [[Jay Shuster]] on [[November 18]], [[1996]], and a one-eighth scale maquette of the entire vehicle was also made.[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']] Mawhonic's vehicle was one of the only full-scale racers built for the starting grid sequence''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]'' so that [[Mark Coulier]], the actor playing the Gran,{{SWArchive|url=episode-i/fun/snapshot/2001/02/snapshot20010214.html|series=Episode I Snapshot|text=Tatooine Tango}} could sit in the reclining seat on top. The podracers were all constructed from surplus military airplane parts in [[Wikipedia:England|England]] over a period of five months and then shipped to [[Wikipedia:Tunisia|Tunisia]] on [[July 17]], [[1997]] to be filmed. However, before they could be filmed, a severe storm hit the area on [[July 30]], damaging all of the shipped podracers to some degree ranging from having parts ripped off to almost complete destruction. The international crew who had been about to return to England remained in Tunisia and were able to repair the damage so that the starting grid scene could be shot in [[Oung Jmel|Chott el Gharsa]] between [[August 5]]-[[August|6]], 1997.''[[The Star Wars Archives: Episodes I–III, 1999–2005]]'' [[File:GPE-3130PodracerCockpitModel-TPMIG.png|thumb|left|250px|A 1/8th scale maquette of a GPE-3130]] In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], the GPE-3130 Podracer was first identified in the [[Star Wars video games|mobile card game]] ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'', which initially launched in [[2013]]. Although the launch of ''Force Collection'' predates{{SW|url=news/announcing-star-wars-force-collection|text=Announcing Star Wars: Force Collection|nolive=1}} the ''Star Wars'' canon reset of [[2014]],{{SW|url=news/the-legendary-star-wars-expanded-universe-turns-a-new-page|text=The Legendary Star Wars Expanded Universe Turns a New Page}} [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Leland Chee]] confirmed that the game was kept updated to fit with canon.{{Twitter|holocronkeeper|status/846807700482666496|[[Leland Chee]]|quote=I'm not gonna go through the trouble of changing them and I don't have any reason to believe currently that anyone would. […] On the off-chance that we DID have a current need to change any of these, we would have for Force Collection.|archivedate=20210505080831}} — [[Leland Chee]] of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] has confirmed that [[in-universe]] information from ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'' conforms with ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]]. The name originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where the name [[GPE-3130 Podracer/Legends|GPE-3130]] was first used in the video game [[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'']],[[Star Wars: Episode I Racer|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Racer'']] which was released on the same day as ''The Phantom Menace''.{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/games/star-wars-episode-i-racer|text=Star Wars: Episode I: Racer - Nintendo 64 - IGN|work=[http://www.ign.com IGN]|archivedate=20200524203904}} ===LEGO Appearances=== {{Quote|[…]Mawhonic in his mean, green machine[…]|Fode introduces Mawhonic in "Exit from Endor"|{{DroidTales|Exit from Endor}}}} [[File:DengarBoardsMawhonic-RoT.png|thumb|right|300px|Dengar boards Mawhonic's GPE-3130 Podracer in "Race on Tatooine."]] Mawhonic's GPE-3130 Podracer is shown in the non-[[canon]] ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures]]'' episode "[[Race on Tatooine]],"{{FreemakerAdventures|Race on Tatooine}} which aired on [[July 18]], 2016.{{YouTube|video=MJnc0s0xt4E|text=Race on Tatooine|channel=show/SC7GMxdyD28jjHoiECG7tOpQ?season=1|name=LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures}} In the episode, Mawhonic uses it to participate in the [[29th Annual Bricklayers' Classic]] podrace on Tatooine, but during the second lap of the race, the [[bounty hunter]] [[Dengar]] leaps aboard the GPE-3130's repulsorpod from the stolen [[IPG-X1131 LongTail]] of racer [[Teemto Pagalies]]. Dengar then leaps from the vehicle onto another pod while trying to reach the vehicle of the [[Freemakers/LEGO|Freemakers]], a family also competing in the race, and during his pursuit he later jumps on and off Mawhonic's vehicle again. Ultimately the Freemakers win the race after besting Dengar. [[File:PodraceStartingGrid-SWS.png|thumb|left|300px|Players can race against Mawhonic's GPE-3130 Podracer in ''LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga''.]] Mawhonic and his vehicle also appears in a non-canon retelling of ''The Phantom Menace'' depicted in "[[Exit from Endor]]," the first episode of ''[[LEGO Star Wars: Droid Tales]]'', which aired on [[July 6]], [[2015]].{{YouTube|video=SGjoPgopLtA|text=Exit from Endor|channel=show/SCkNhajeNrARRe7MtuN5T36Q?season=1|name=LEGO Star Wars: Droid Tales}} In the episode, Mawhonic and the GPE-3130 Podracer make it as far as the second lap of the Boonta Eve Classic, where Mawhonic rams his engines into the [[Anakin Skywalker's Podracer|vehicle]] of Skywalker. Skywalker then swings his engines back into the GPE-3130, which sends Mawhonic and the podracer spiralling into the sky where the GPE-3130 explodes, showering parts down into the sand near a the sun-bathing [[Jedi]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. In the [[2022]] video game ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]'', Mawhonic once again pilots the GPE-3130 during the Boonta Eve Classic depicted in ''The Phantom Menace'', but crashes before even reaching Mushroom Mesa. Players can later encounter Mawhonic in the [[city]] of [[Mos Espa]], where he complains that Sebulba always manages to destroy his pod. In the quest "Pod Parts Procurement" he then asks the player to bring him super tough [[bone]] from the planet [[Utapau]] so he can construct a new, more resilient pod.''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]'' ==Appearances== *{{Film|I}} {{1st}} *[[Star Wars: The Phantom Menace Graphic Novel Adaptation|''Star Wars: The Phantom Menace'' Graphic Novel Adaptation]] *''[[Star Wars: The Prequel Trilogy – A Graphic Novel]]'' *''[[Star Wars Journeys: The Phantom Menace]]'' *''[[Star Wars Journeys: Beginnings]]'' *{{StoryCite|story=The Path of a Podracer|book=The Prequel Trilogy Stories|audiobook=1}} ===Non-canon appearances=== *{{DroidTales|Exit from Endor}} {{Flash}} *{{FreemakerAdventures|Race on Tatooine}} *''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga]]'' ==Sources== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of GPE-3130 Podracers}} *''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' *{{HelmetCollectionCite|17|Weapons & Uniforms}} *''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'' *[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] {{Po}} *''[[Endless Vigil]]'' {{1stID|3130-series factory custom}} *''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' *''[[Star Wars Super Graphic: A Visual Guide to a Galaxy Far, Far Away]]'' *''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A -
